root_cause.text: The Hyper-V PCI driver’s hv_pci_probe() error path manually released hbus->bridge->domain_nr even after assigning it to the host bridge, while the PCI core later freed the same emulated domain number again in pci_release_host_bridge_dev(), causing a double ida_free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the explicit error-path call `pci_bus_release_emul_domain_nr(hbus->bridge->domain_nr)` from `drivers/pci/controller/pci-hyperv.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that after storing the domain number in `hbus->bridge->domain_nr`, cleanup via `pci_release_host_bridge_dev()` also frees it, leading to `ida_free called for id=... which is not allocated`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the workqueue-allocation failure path in `hv_pci_probe` to clean up bus resources correctly before releasing the domain.
intent_record.what: The error-handling branch after checking `if (!hbus->wq)` was changed to jump to `free_bus` instead of `free_dom` when `alloc_ordered_workqueue()` fails and `ret` is set to `-ENOMEM`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if workqueue allocation fails during `hv_pci_probe`, cleanup now follows a later error path that also frees the bus-related allocation instead of skipping directly to domain cleanup, preventing leaked bus resources and ensuring proper teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop releasing the emulated PCI domain number in this hv_pci_probe() failure path to avoid incorrect cleanup on probe error.
intent_record.what: The error-handling path in hv_pci_probe() was changed by removing the free_dom label and deleting the call to pci_bus_release_emul_domain_nr(hbus->bridge->domain_nr) before the existing free_bus cleanup.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this error path no longer releases the emulated PCI domain number when probe fails after the workqueue is destroyed and before the bus structure is freed, preventing that cleanup action from occurring in this failure case.

grouping_result.intent: Stop releasing the emulated PCI domain number in this hv_pci_probe() failure path to avoid incorrect cleanup on probe error.

consistency_review.core_intent: Correct hv_pci_probe() failure-path cleanup so bus resources are cleaned up appropriately without incorrectly releasing the emulated PCI domain.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the hv_pci_probe() error-path cleanup and specifically remove the manual release of the emulated PCI domain number, which is the exact cause of the double ida_free when the PCI core later frees it.

candidates.rationale: This manually frees the emulated PCI domain number on the hv_pci_probe() error path even though ownership had already been transferred to the host bridge, so the PCI core later frees it again during host bridge release, causing the double ida_free.
This routes the allocation-failure path into the incorrect cleanup label that manually releases the emulated domain number, directly triggering the double-free condition.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct root cause: it manually frees the emulated PCI domain number after ownership was already assigned to the host bridge, so the PCI core later frees the same domain again during host bridge release, resulting in a double ida_free.

This statement sends the workqueue-allocation failure path to the cleanup label that executes the manual domain-number release, thereby triggering the incorrect second free described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact probe-time assignment of the PCI domain number into the host bridge and the corresponding error path cleanup. In hv_pci_probe(), the new line `hbus->bridge->domain_nr = dom;` assigns the emulated domain number to the `pci_host_bridge`. Later, in the probe error path label `free_dom:`, the code explicitly calls `hv_put_dom_num(hbus->bridge->domain_nr);`. This matches the described root cause: after the domain number has been assigned to the host bridge, the driver still manually releases it on probe failure. Since the PCI core will later free `bridge->domain_nr` in host bridge release, this creates the double-free condition. The commit message even says this is 'No functional change', and nothing in the shown code adds protective handling to avoid freeing the domain twice. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it contains the full probe error path and the domain allocation/release logic. The root cause describes a double free caused when hv_pci_probe() manually released `hbus->bridge->domain_nr` after the domain had already been assigned to the PCI host bridge, and then the PCI core freed it again in `pci_release_host_bridge_dev()`. In this snippet, there is no assignment to `hbus->bridge->domain_nr`, no host bridge object setup visible, and no error path that frees `hbus->bridge->domain_nr`. Instead, the function allocates a domain number early (`dom = hv_get_dom_num(dom_req);`, `hbus->sysdata.domain = dom;`) and on pre-host-bridge failures releases only that private reservation via `hv_put_dom_num(hbus->sysdata.domain);` at label `free_dom:`. Since the vulnerable construct specifically requires manually freeing the host bridge's `domain_nr` after ownership was transferred to the PCI core, and that construct is absent here, `has_bug` is false. The code already reflects the corrected handling model for this function body: only the driver's own domain reservation is released in this pre-bridge error path, not a host bridge domain number that would later be freed by the PCI core.
